doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Monk, Ellington and Archie Shepp in the 1970s
title: Red Garland, Archie Shepp in Philadelphia and meeting Gloria
summary: Ware plays with Red Garland and then with Shepp's band in Philadelphia, where he meets his wife Gloria.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: During this period, Red Garland comes through New York. Philly Jimmy Joe Jones, myself and Red Garland played a little East Side joint, little jazz joint, up in the 90s. That place was really diggin' it, but cat wouldn't take care of business. The cat would come in at 12:00 and play until three and that was it, you know. So, that didn't last long and Archie Shepp had some more (unintelligible) gigs for me. He say, "Well, come on, Wilbur, let's go down to Philly" -- about 72 -- and coming down here to play at a place called Aqua Lounge over in West Philly. Archie had Maged, Charles Greenlee on trombone. He had Dave Burrell on piano and Joe Masontos (PHONETIC) on congar and
Ottie on congas and Beaver Harris on drums. That was his band.

I hadn't been down there since the '60s. But I played. We played that weekend and that's where I met my wife Gloria. She was sitting there at the bar, loved music and we talked for -- a musician that knew me introduced me to her. I didn't know she was a schoolteacher or nothing like that. She was just a lady and kind enough to put -- she knew Dave Burrell. She knew Dave and his wife. So, she said, "Well, instead of commuting back to New York, why don't you stay out at my house?" I said, "Me, too?" She said, "Of course." So, we come and spent the weekend with her. I told her, "If you ever come to New York, look me up," you know. I'd like to repay her for her hospitality.
That's what happened. That was our meeting, we've been together just about ever since then. That's for you, honey.
